plan.contextChunk: This figure shows the geometry of light refraction at a planar interface between two optical media, as described by Snell's law. A horizontal black line divides the scene into an upper region with refractive index n1 and a lower region with refractive index n2; a thick blue line traces the ray direction as it strikes the interface and continues into the second medium. A thin vertical line marks the surface normal at the point of incidence, with a small right-angle square confirming its perpendicularity to the interface; the angle theta_1 is measured between the incoming ray and the normal above the interface, and theta_2 is measured between the refracted ray and the normal below. The ray bends toward or away from the normal depending on the relative magnitudes of n1 and n2, embodying the relationship n1 sin theta_1 = n2 sin theta_2. This figure introduces refraction geometry as the physical basis for how lenses bend light and form images.

interactionPlan.concept: Snell's law, n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2), fixes how a ray bends at a planar interface: it bends toward the normal entering a denser medium, away from it entering a rarer one, and beyond the critical angle (n1 > n2) refraction becomes impossible and the ray totally internally reflects.
elements: horizontal black interface line spanning the full width, dividing upper medium n1 from lower medium n2
label 'n1' in the upper-left region
label 'n2' in the lower-left region
thin cyan vertical surface-normal line through the point of incidence
label 'surface normal' at the top of the normal line
small right-angle square marker at the interface/normal intersection confirming perpendicularity
thick blue incident ray from upper-left to the incidence point, labeled 'ray direction' (rotated along the ray)
thick blue refracted ray continuing from the incidence point into the lower medium
angle arc and label 'theta1' between the incident ray and the normal above the interface
angle arc and label 'theta2' between the refracted ray and the normal below the interface
reflected ray (shown only during total internal reflection) leaving the incidence point symmetrically above the interface
critical-angle indicator / annotation shown when n1 > n2

interactions.teaches: Rotating the incident ray about the incidence point changes theta1, and theta2 is forced to track it through n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2) — the refracted ray is not free, it is determined by the law

interactions.label: n1 (upper medium)
interactions.teaches: Raising n1 above n2 makes the lower medium optically rarer, so the refracted ray bends away from the normal and a critical angle appears beyond which total internal reflection occurs

interactions.label: n2 (lower medium)
interactions.teaches: Increasing n2 relative to n1 bends the refracted ray closer to the surface normal, showing that a denser second medium pulls the ray toward the normal

demo_steps.title: Refraction toward the normal
demo_steps.narration: With n2 > n1 the ray enters a denser medium and bends toward the normal, so theta2 is smaller than theta1. The two angle arcs and the ray geometry obey n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2).

demo_steps.title: Drag the incident ray
demo_steps.narration: Drag the blue incident ray to sweep theta1 from near 0 to near 90 degrees; theta2 updates in real time and the refracted ray swings accordingly, making the sine relationship visible rather than abstract.

demo_steps.title: Bend away from the normal
demo_steps.narration: Now set n1 > n2 so the ray enters a rarer medium: the refracted ray bends away from the normal (theta2 > theta1), the opposite of the first case.

demo_steps.title: Total internal reflection
demo_steps.narration: Keep n1 > n2 and drag theta1 past the critical angle: no real theta2 satisfies Snell's law, the refracted ray vanishes below the interface, and a reflected ray appears symmetrically above it — total internal reflection.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The refracted ray's angle is not arbitrary — it is locked to the incident angle by n1 sin(theta1) = n2 sin(theta2), and when n1 > n2 this equation simply has no solution past the critical angle, which is exactly why total internal reflection happens.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Center the incidence point on a full-width horizontal black interface line; label n1 above-left and n2 below-left. Draw a thin cyan vertical normal through the incidence point with a small right-angle square at the junction and a 'surface normal' label at its top. The incident ray is a thick blue line from the upper-left to the point with a rotated 'ray direction' label; the refracted ray is a thick blue line from the point into the lower medium. Render theta1 and theta2 as small angle arcs with Greek-letter labels between each ray and the normal. Default state should match the source image (ray bending toward the normal, n2 > n1). On total internal reflection, hide the refracted ray, draw a reflected ray mirroring the incident ray above the interface, and optionally mark the critical angle on the upper side. Cross-fade the reflected/refracted rays at the critical angle rather than popping them.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Drag the incident ray to change θ₁ and watch θ₂ update in real time according to n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂, with both angle arc labels refreshing as the ray rotates about the interface point
- Sliders for refractive indices n₁ and n₂: show how increasing n₂ relative to n₁ bends the refracted ray closer to the surface normal, and vice versa
- Increase n₁ above n₂ and drag θ₁ past the critical angle to trigger total internal reflection, showing the refracted ray disappear below the interface and a reflected ray appear symmetrically above it

discrepancies: The generated figure draws small black angle arcs for θ₁ and θ₂, whereas the source uses bare text labels with no arc curves
A right-docked control panel (narration, step buttons, two sliders) shifts the optical diagram leftward, altering the centered composition of the source

evaluation.notes: A faithful, conceptually exact Snell's-law refraction figure: correct interface, cyan normal, blue incident/refracted rays bending toward the normal, right-angle marker, and all source labels (n₁, n₂, θ₁, θ₂, surface normal, ray direction) are present, and the added n₁/n₂ sliders, draggable incident ray, and 4-step demo (including correct total internal reflection past the critical angle) are all functional and pedagogically strong; only minor additions (angle arcs, right-docked panel, smaller θ glyphs) deviate from the static source.
action_items: Optionally remove or lighten the θ₁/θ₂ angle arcs (or make them toggleable) to match the source's bare-label style and reduce clutter near the vertex
Increase the on-figure θ₁/θ₂ font size to better match the prominent θ glyphs in the source and preserve label hierarchy
Verify the rotated 'ray direction' label does not collide with the incident ray or the θ₁ arc at small θ₁ values during dragging
